elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence caps "each Party's total aggregate liability to the other Parties arising out of or in connection with this Agreement" — party-neutral and therefore mutual across all Parties, including us.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is only "the fees paid or payable by that Party ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim"; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. Drafter expressly declined the floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 21.3: "Under no circumstances shall any Party be liable to any other Party ... for any indirect or consequential loss or damage" — mutual and left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out lead-in: "Except in respect of ... its breach of Paragraph 31 (Confidentiality)" — confidentiality breach sits outside the cap (the parenthetical identifies the subject matter).

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list names only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations are excepted from the cap.
"Except in respect of a Party's indemnification obligations under Subparagraph 21.2" — the 21.2 third-party indemnity is outside the new cap (its Schedule B share limit is unaffected).
Fraud does not appear in the carve-out lead-in or anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out; the exception list stops at wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language stating that amounts payable by us (contributions/fees) are not "damages" or are outside the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability to the other Parties ... shall not exceed" — symmetrical wording binding every Party.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by that Party under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — a 12-months-fees basis.
Lead-in excepts "a Party's indemnification obligations under Subparagraph 21.2" from the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: one inserted sentence delivers a mutual cap on a 12-months-fees basis with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct expressly outside the cap.

Preferred is not reached (no USD 1,000,000 floor; no data protection/security, fraud, IP-infringement carve-outs; no Customer-payment-obligations exclusion). That is acceptable because the finding targets the fallback level, and the drafter says so in the comment.

Minimality holds: the redline is a single concise insertion at 21.4 with no deletions, no paraphrase of 21.2 or 21.3, and no extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedures, no additional damages categories).

Intent preserved: the 21.2 Schedule B share limitation and the mutual 21.3 indirect/consequential exclusion survive intact, and because indemnity is carved out of the new cap there is no contradiction between the Schedule B share limit and the 12-months-fees cap.

Repair advisory (not an element failure): confirm that Paragraph 31 is in fact the confidentiality paragraph in this Agreement — if the numbering is wrong the carve-out becomes a dangling cross-reference; consider "its breach of its confidentiality obligations" to remove the dependency.

Repair advisory (not an element failure): "fees paid or payable by that Party" could yield a nil or near-nil cap for any Party that pays no fees under the Agreement, effectively immunising a counterparty against us. Consider "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement" (or referencing Schedule B contributions) so the cap has substance in both directions.
